title: Verify premature rounding after the merged USGS economic-unit correction
problem: The economic impact caller multiplies by one million after its shared midpoint helper has already truncated to an integer, losing fractional millions. The original unit fix is already merged; this is a separate precision edge case.
humanitarian_relevance: Avoiding misleading zero or coarsened economic impact values has a pathway to clearer disaster analysis. Frequency, downstream reliance and actual benefit are unmeasured.

evidence.claim: PR #204 merged on 2026-08-31 and current source contains people/usd normalization and a one-million scale factor. Do not duplicate the original unit fix.

Hash-checked original arithmetic returns 0 for a synthetic 0.5-million midpoint and 5 million for a 5.5-million midpoint; scaling the same formula before integer conversion preserves 500000 and 5500000 respectively. Two control cases agree. No full transformer or production test ran.

Premature truncation can erase a nonzero value or discard up to almost one million dollars under the current nonnegative midpoint arithmetic. This does not validate that aggregation model or establish a real-world loss-estimation error.

Three full-transformer synthetic cases emitted the previously predicted rounded economic values while fatality and country controls held. All 8 existing USGS tests passed with networking blocked. No target code was changed; runtime warnings and limits are recorded.
GitHub returned the exact prepared inquiry authored by humanifest-bot at 2026-09-09T01:18:23Z. This establishes delivery only; no maintainer acceptance is claimed.

Original arithmetic on the archived public economic bins yields 1768846000000 USD versus 1768846489394 with Decimal scale-before-rounding. The 489394 difference is about 0.000028%; neither output is asserted to be ground-truth loss or a validated model.

code_surface: pystac_monty/sources/usgs.py economic caller and _calculate_value_from_bins; validators/usgs.py AlertBin; tests/extensions/test_usgs.py and tests/data/usgs/venezuela_alerts.json.
proposed_change: Seek confirmation for a focused economic precision correction: scale before integer rounding while preserving fatality values and empty/error behavior. The full item output reproduces the problem. Add acceptance tests for 500000 and 5500000 USD plus controls after all hard gates pass; do not revive the paused loss-model redesign.
tests: Executed 3 real-transformer reproduction cases with networking blocked: emitted economic values 0, 5000000 and 1000000 USD; unchanged fatality control 139 people and VEN country. All 8 existing USGS tests passed offline. Probe checks current faulty behavior, not acceptance of a fix. Earlier 4 arithmetic cases also passed; whole-project suite and production behavior not tested. Extended arithmetic probe also passes on one hash-checked archived USGS payload; its small relative difference is not evidence of consequential real-world loss error.
